title: Preparation of chaperone-loaded neural stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles for Huntington's disease
author: Joshi, Zuhorn

This protocol explains the filter trap assay, which separates aggregated (insoluble) proteins from soluble proteins. Shortly, cell lysates (Figure 6) are passed through the cellulose acetate membrane which traps aggregates >200 nm, separating them from soluble proteins (Figure 7). The trapped proteins can be detected, which enables semiquantitative measurements for protein aggregation.88.Place coverslips in 6 well plates as described in 40–48.89.Trypsinize Hek293T cells, count and seed 15 × 104 cells in complete medium per well and incubate for 24 h at 37°C.90.Transfect with 1 μg pEGFP-Q74 (encoding HTT-Q74-GFP) using JetPEI® (Polyplus,10110-N) for 4 h following the manufacturer’s protocol.91.Rinse the cells rigorously with HBSS. steps.title: Prepare DNAJB6 expression plasmids
steps.instruction: Amplify GFP and GFP‑DNAJB6 fragments, digest fragments and vector, purify, ligate, transform, screen colonies, miniprep, and sequence the resulting plasmids.

substeps.instruction: Purchase XPack™ CMV‑XP‑MCS‑EF1‑Puro lentivector (catalog XPAK510PA‑1, SBI Biosciences).

PCR amplify GFP and GFP‑DNAJB6b using pcDNA5/FRT/TO GFP‑DNAJB6b (Addgene #19501) with the following 50 µL master mix: DNA template 100 ng (1 µL), Herculase II fusion DNA polymerase (0.5 µL), Primer 1 (10 µM, 1.25 µL), Primer 2 or 3 (10 µM, 1.25 µL), 5× Herculase II buffer (10 µL), 25 mM dNTP mix (0.5 µL), ddH₂O to 50 µL. Cycle: 95 °C 2 min; 25–35 × (95 °C 10 s, 60 °C 20 s, 72 °C 30 s per kb); 72 °C 3 min; hold 4 °C.

Digest PCR products and the lentiviral backbone with XhoI‑HF and EcoRI‑HF in 50 µL: CutSmart buffer (10×, 5 µL), DNA (10 µg equivalent), XhoI (1.5 µL), EcoRI (1.5 µL), ddH₂O to 50 µL; incubate 37 °C 2 h.
Purify digested fragments using QIAquick PCR & Gel Cleanup Kit.
Run the digested vector on a 200 V agarose gel, excise the larger band (vector backbone), and gel‑purify as above.

Ligate inserts into the cut vector (50 µL total): NEB ligation buffer (10×, 5 µL), NEB ligase (10 µg equiv.), cut vector (100 ng, 1.5 µL), PCR insert (50 ng, 1.5 µL), ddH₂O to 50 µL; incubate RT 10 min.
Transform ligation mix into DH5α competent cells, plate on LB‑ampicillin agar, incubate 18 h at 37 °C.

Screen 10 colonies by colony PCR using Green GoTaq (Promega) with 10 µL master mix: 5× GoTaq buffer (2 µL), Primer 1 (0.1 µL, 10 µM), Primer 2 or 3 (0.1 µL, 10 µM), GoTaq polymerase (0.1 µL), 10 mM dNTP mix (0.2 µL), ddH₂O to 10 µL; add colony scrap. Cycle: 95 °C 2 min; 25–35 × (95 °C 30 s, 60 °C 30 s, 72 °C 1 min per kb); 72 °C 5 min; hold 4 °C.
Select three clones with correct band sizes, inoculate each in 3 mL LB‑ampicillin, grow overnight 37 °C.
Isolate plasmid DNA with Promega miniprep kit.
Send plasmids for Sanger sequencing; keep the clone with no insert mutations.
Resulting vectors: pCMV‑XP‑GFP‑EF1‑Puro and pCMV‑XP‑GFP‑DNAJB6‑EF1‑Puro.

steps.title: Prepare exosome‑depleted complete medium
steps.instruction: Ultracentrifuge fetal bovine serum to remove endogenous extracellular vesicles and filter‑sterilize the supernatant.

substeps.instruction: Prepare DMEM containing 10 % FBS and 1 % penicillin‑streptomycin.

Spray the inner and outer surfaces of 38.5 mL ultracentrifuge (UC) tubes (Certified Free Open‑Top Thinwall Polypropylene, 25 × 89 mm, 50 Pk, C14285) and Beckman SW32i rotor tubes with ample 70 % ethanol; let dry under a laminar flow hood.
Add medium to each UC tube leaving ~2 cm from the tube edge, cap tightly, and place tubes in balanced holders.
Balance tubes (add or remove medium as needed) with caps closed.
Ultracentrifuge at 110 000 g for 16 h at 4 °C using a Sorvall Discovery 90SE (SW32i rotor).
Collect the supernatant carefully, filter through a 0.2 µm syringe filter, and store at 4 °C for up to 2 weeks.
Alternative: ultracentrifuge 100 % FBS under the same conditions, store the supernatant at –80 °C for long‑term use (note: higher viscosity may precipitate proteins and affect cell viability).

steps.title: Prepare complete medium for cell culture
steps.instruction: Make DMEM supplemented with serum and antibiotics for routine cell maintenance.

substeps.instruction: Combine DMEM with 10 % fetal bovine serum, 5 % horse serum, and 1 % penicillin‑streptomycin.
Mix thoroughly and store at 4 °C for a maximum of 2 months or until the medium turns red (indicating alkalinity).

steps.title: Subculture C17.2 neural stem cells
steps.instruction: Thaw, seed, and grow C17.2 cells in complete medium before EV collection.

substeps.instruction: Subculture C17.2 cells in the complete medium prepared above and incubate overnight until cells adhere to the flask surface.
The next day rinse the monolayer twice with Hank's Balanced Salt Solution (HBSS).
Add the exosome‑depleted medium (prepared in step 2) to the cells and incubate for 2 days before EV isolation.

steps.title: Condition cells for EV collection
steps.instruction: Wash confluent C17.2 cultures and add exosome‑depleted medium to generate EV‑rich conditioned media.

substeps.instruction: After overnight incubation cells should be ~60 % confluent; wash twice with HBSS.
Add 20 mL exosome‑depleted medium to each T162 flask (covers the surface) to concentrate the sEV sample.
Maintain cells at ~60 % confluency; avoid over‑growth to prevent differentiation. Two days incubation yields ~2 µg/µL sEVs from ten T162 flasks (≈50 µL total).

steps.title: Generate stable C17.2 lines overexpressing DNAJB6
steps.instruction: Use nucleofection and a paper‑disc cloning method to create monoclonal C17.2 lines expressing XPack‑tagged GFP‑DNAJB6.

substeps.instruction: Seed 2–3 × 10⁶ C17.2 cells per 15 cm dish (one dish per plasmid) and incubate overnight at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ to reach 3–4 × 10⁶ cells (~80 % confluency).
Remove medium, wash once with DPBS (volume equal to the removed medium).
Detach cells with trypsin/EDTA at 37 °C for 3 min until fully detached.
Add complete medium, pipette to obtain a homogeneous single‑cell suspension, and take 10 µL for counting with a hemocytometer.
Centrifuge 1 × 10⁶ cells at 200 g for 10 min at room temperature.
Prepare nucleofection mix: add the supplied supplement solution to the Lonza Nucleofector™ Solution.
Start the 4D‑Nucleofector™ (Lonza), load the DN‑100 program (use 100 µL nucleocuvette™).
Pre‑warm 10 mL complete medium in each 10 cm plate (one plate per condition) and equilibrate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.
Resuspend the cell pellet in room‑temperature Nucleofector™ Solution, add 5 µg plasmid DNA (≤10 % of final volume), and transfer to a nucleocuvette™.
Electroporate using the DN‑100 program, then immediately add the electroporated cells to the pre‑warmed 10 cm plates.
Incubate cells; apply antibiotic selection (puromycin) as required to enrich transfectants (selection details not specified).
Monoclonal isolation via paper‑disc method:
a. Remove parafilm from the dish, warm trypsin, and place 12–15 autoclaved paper discs in the lid.
b. Distribute 500 µL complete medium per well in a labeled 24‑well plate.
c. Under a laminar flow hood, wash the dish twice with HBSS, flame tweezers twice, let cool.
d. Dip a paper disc in trypsin/EDTA, place on an encircled colony, and incubate 3 min at 37 °C.
e. Transfer the disc (with attached cells) to a designated well of the 24‑well plate; rinse the well with medium using a fresh 1 mL tip.
f. Repeat for all visible colonies, then place the 24‑well plate in the incubator.
g. Monitor daily; colonies become visible after 4–5 days. When wells reach ~70 % confluence, discard the paper discs and transfer cells to a 6‑well plate.
h. After colonies expand, screen for GFP and GFP‑DNAJB6 fluorescence; select clones with the highest expression and correct plasma‑membrane/endosomal localization.
i. Expand each selected clone in a 10 cm dish to ~80 % confluence, then split to three 10 cm dishes.
j. Freeze cells from two dishes in five cryogenic vials (standard freezing medium).
k. Keep the remaining dish for downstream EV production.

steps.title: Immunostain donor cell lines
steps.instruction: Detect exosome marker proteins in WT, XP‑GFP, and XP‑GFP‑DNAJB6b C17.2 cells by immunofluorescence.

substeps.instruction: Trypsinize WT, XP‑GFP, and XP‑GFP‑DNAJB6b cells, count, and seed 3 × 10⁴ cells per well onto glass coverslips placed in a 24‑well plate; incubate 24 h at 37 °C.
Fix cells with 4 % paraformaldehyde in PBS for 30 min at room temperature; wash twice with PBS.
Permeabilize with 0.2 % Tween‑20 in PBS for 5 min at room temperature; rinse with PBS.
Block with 3 % BSA in PBS for 1 h at room temperature.
Incubate with primary anti‑CD9 antibody diluted 1:200 in blocking buffer overnight at 4 °C (alternatives: CD63, ALIX, TSG101, HSP90).
Next day, rinse three times with PBS and incubate with secondary antibody (1:500) plus DAPI in blocking buffer for 30 min at room temperature.

Rinse with PBS, mount coverslips on microscope slides using Faramount mounting medium, and image with a Leica SP8 confocal microscope (63× oil, NA 1.4; excitation/emission settings: DiI 551/565 nm, DAPI 358/463 nm, GFP 490/544 nm).

steps.title: Isolate small extracellular vesicles from culture
steps.instruction: Collect conditioned medium from high‑expressing C17.2 clones and purify sEVs by sequential centrifugation and ultracentrifugation.

substeps.instruction: Seed 3–5 × 10⁶ C17.2 donor cells (XP‑GFP or XP‑GFP‑DNAJB6) per 10 T162 flask in 20 mL complete medium; incubate overnight at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.
The next day, wash cells with HBSS and add 20 mL exosome‑depleted medium (cells should be ~40 % confluent).
After 48 h, collect the conditioned medium (~180 mL) into five 38.5 mL ultracentrifuge tubes (≈36 mL per tube).
Add an equal volume of sterile water to one tube for balancing; weigh tubes and adjust to balance.
Centrifuge at 500 g for 10 min at 4 °C; transfer supernatant to a fresh tube without disturbing the pellet.
Centrifuge the supernatant at 2 000 g for 10 min at 4 °C (Beckman Coulter Allegra X‑15R); transfer supernatant to a fresh UC tube.
Centrifuge at 10 000 g for 30 min at 4 °C using a Sorvall Discovery 90SE (SW32i rotor) to remove apoptotic vesicles and microvesicles.
Ultracentrifuge the resulting supernatant at 110 000 g for 70 min at 4 °C (Beckman SW55i rotor) to pellet sEVs.
Resuspend the pellet in 5 mL cold DPBS, transfer to a new 14 mL UC tube (Certified Free Open‑Top Thinwall Polypropylene, 14 × 95 mm), and ultracentrifuge again at 110 000 g for 70 min at 4 °C.
Resuspend the final pellet in 50 µL cold DPBS and store at 4 °C for downstream assays.

steps.title: Perform filter trap assay for protein aggregates
steps.instruction: Treat HEK293T cells with sEVs, lyse, and capture aggregated proteins on a cellulose acetate membrane using a Bio‑Dot apparatus.

substeps.instruction: Place glass coverslips (as prepared in step 6) into 6‑well plates.
Trypsinize HEK293T cells, count, and seed 1.5 × 10⁵ cells per well in complete medium; incubate 24 h at 37 °C.
Transfect each well with 1 µg pEGFP‑Q74 (HTT‑Q74‑GFP) using JetPEI® (Polyplus, 10110‑N) for 4 h according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Rinse cells thoroughly with HBSS (multiple washes to avoid loss of loosely attached cells).
Add 100 µg total sEV protein (diluted to 50 µg/mL in 1 mL exosome‑depleted medium) to each well; incubate 36 h. Include a control well receiving exosome‑depleted medium only.
After incubation, rinse cells once with HBSS.
Add 400 µL filter‑trap assay (FTA) buffer per well (10 mM Tris‑Cl pH 8.0, 150 mM NaCl, 2 % SDS).
Scrape cells, transfer the viscous lysate to a 1 mL pipette tip (200 µL tips are insufficient).
Sonicate the lysates, then determine protein concentration with the Bio‑Rad DC protein assay kit.
Dilute lysates in assay buffer to 1 µg/µL (final volume 285 µL).
Add 15 µL of 1 M DTT to each sample (final volume 300 µL).
Heat samples at 95 °C for 5 min (samples can be stored at –80 °C for later use).
Set up the Bio‑Dot SF apparatus (Bio‑Rad 1706542): clean, prepare 50 mL FTA wash buffer (10 mM Tris‑Cl pH 8.0, 150 mM NaCl, 0.1 % SDS).
Soak two thick Trans‑blot papers and a 0.2 µm cellulose acetate membrane in wash buffer; place membrane on the papers in the apparatus.
Remove air bubbles by gently rolling a 10 mL plastic pipette over the membrane.
Close the lid, tighten screws diagonally, apply full vacuum, then tighten further under vacuum.
Add 200 µL wash buffer, apply vacuum until it passes through; repeat once.
Add 100 µL of each sample to the corresponding well, apply low vacuum carefully and allow the buffer to pass completely.
Wash the slots three times with 200 µL wash buffer each, ensuring all buffer is removed.
Block the membrane in 20 mL Odyssey Blocking Buffer for 1 h at room temperature on a shaker.
Rinse briefly with PBS‑T, then incubate with anti‑GFP primary antibody (1:2000 in Odyssey Blocking Buffer) overnight at 4 °C on a shaker.
Wash membrane 4 × 10 min with PBS‑T.
Incubate with Odyssey secondary antibody (1:5000 in Odyssey Blocking Buffer) for 1 h at room temperature on a shaker.
Wash 4 × 10 min with PBS‑T.
Detect trapped aggregates using the Odyssey Infrared Imaging System.

steps.title: Perform western blot analysis of protein aggregation
steps.instruction: Run SDS‑PAGE of sEV‑treated cell lysates, transfer to PVDF, and quantify aggregated GFP‑HTT using ImageJ.

substeps.instruction: Take 30 µg of total protein from the lysates prepared in step 9 (after heating) and load onto an SDS‑PAGE gel (follow steps 61‑74 of the original protocol for gel preparation).

Run the gel, then transfer the entire gel (including the stacking gel, which traps large aggregates) onto a PVDF membrane; handle the stacking gel gently to avoid tearing and reposition well walls if needed.
Stain or image the membrane as required; store the membrane at –80 °C if not processed immediately.
Analyze the blot with ImageJ:
a. Draw a rectangle of identical size around each band.
b. Use Analyze > Measure to obtain band intensities.
c. Calculate the percentage of protein aggregation relative to the control sample.

description: This protocol describes methods for isolating small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) from neural stem cell line C17.2 overexpressing the chaperone protein DNAJB6b and studying the effect of these sEVs on protein aggregation in in vitro cellular models of Huntington’s disease.
